1.1.title: Senior management commitment and continual improvement
1.1.guide_reminder: The section shall demonstrate senior management commitment to implementing the Packaging Materials Standard and continual improvement of product safety, quality management, and product safety and quality culture.

coverage_items.label: Policy and communication
coverage_items.reminder: Mention the documented policy, senior approval/signature, communication to personnel, and continual improvement / product safety and quality culture commitment.
coverage_items.original_text:
1.1.1 The site shall maintain a documented policy which states the site’s intention to meet its obligation to produce safe and legally compliant products to the specified quality and confirms its responsibility to its customers. This shall:
• be signed by the person with overall responsibility for the site
• be communicated to all personnel
• include commitment to continuously improve the site’s product safety and quality culture.

coverage_items.label: Product safety and quality culture plan
coverage_items.reminder: Mention the culture plan, activities, measurement, review/update frequency and effectiveness review.
coverage_items.original_text:
1.1.2 The site’s senior management shall define and maintain a clear and effective plan for the development and continuing improvement of a product safety and quality culture. The plan shall include measures needed to achieve a positive culture change.
This shall include:
• defined activities which aim to improve and further develop product safety and quality culture. As a minimum, these activities shall be designed around:
• clear and open communication of product safety
• training
• feedback from personnel
• the behaviours required to maintain and improve product safety processes
• performance measurement of activities related to the safety, legality and quality of products
• an action plan indicating how the activities will be undertaken and measured, and the intended timescales
• a review of the effectiveness of completed and ongoing activities.
The plan shall be reviewed and updated, at a minimum, annually.

coverage_items.label: Confidential reporting system
coverage_items.reminder: Mention confidential concern reporting, communication to personnel and management assessment/action records.
coverage_items.original_text:
1.1.3 The company shall have a confidential reporting system to enable personnel to report concerns relating to product safety, legality, and quality.
The mechanism for reporting concerns shall be clearly communicated to all personnel.
The company’s senior management shall have a process for assessing any concerns raised. Records of the assessment and, where appropriate, actions taken, shall be documented.

coverage_items.label: Objectives and monitoring
coverage_items.reminder: Mention documented objectives for safety, legality and quality, communication, monitoring frequency and results/trends.
coverage_items.original_text:
1.1.4 The site’s senior management shall establish clear objectives to maintain and improve the safety, legality and quality of products manufactured, in accordance with the site’s product safety and quality policy and this Standard. These objectives shall be:
• documented and include targets or clear measures of success
• clearly communicated to relevant personnel
• monitored, and the results reported at a suitable predetermined frequency to the site’s senior management.

coverage_items.label: Human and financial resources
coverage_items.reminder: Mention that senior management provides adequate human and financial resources.
coverage_items.original_text: 1.1.5 The company’s senior management shall provide the human and financial resources required for the manufacture of safe and legally compliant products, to the required quality, and in compliance with the requirements of this Standard.

coverage_items.label: Legislation and technical developments
coverage_items.reminder: Mention how the site keeps informed of and reviews scientific/technical developments, industry codes and applicable legislation.
coverage_items.original_text:
1.1.6 The company’s senior management shall have a system in place to ensure that the site is kept informed of and reviews:
• scientific and technical developments
• industry codes of practice
• all relevant legislation applicable in the country of manufacture and, where known, the country where the product will be used.

coverage_items.label: Current Standard access and BRCGS updates
coverage_items.reminder: Mention access to the current Standard and awareness of BRCGS website/Participate updates.
coverage_items.original_text: 1.1.7 The site shall have a genuine, original hard copy or electronic version of the current Standard and be aware of any changes to the Standard or protocol that are published on the BRCGS website and Participate.

coverage_items.label: Recertification audit timing
coverage_items.reminder: Mention that recertification audit planning meets the due date and protocol expectations.
coverage_items.original_text:
1.1.8 Where the site is certificated to the Standard, it shall ensure that announced or blended announced re-certification audits occur on or before the audit due date indicated on the certificate.
It is the site’s responsibility to ensure that all requirements are in place to ensure that the unannounced audit can be undertaken in accordance with the protocol of the Standard (see Part III, section 4.7.1). This includes agreeing contractual terms with the certification body in advance of the start of the 4-month window, and keeping the certification body up to date on changes that may affect this planning, such as maintenance shutdowns.

coverage_items.label: Opening and closing meeting attendance
coverage_items.reminder: Mention senior operations/senior management attendance at opening/closing meetings and availability of relevant managers.
coverage_items.original_text:
1.1.9 The most senior manufacturing or operations manager on site shall participate in the opening and closing meetings of the audit for certification to the Standard.
Relevant departmental managers or their deputies shall be available as required during the audit.
A member of the senior management team on site shall be available during the audit for a discussion on effective implementation of the product safety and quality culture plan.

coverage_items.label: Previous non-conformities and root causes
coverage_items.reminder: Mention that root causes and corrective actions from previous audit non-conformities were effectively addressed.
coverage_items.original_text: 1.1.10 The site’s senior management shall ensure that the root causes of any non-conformities identified at the previous audit against the Standard have been effectively addressed to prevent recurrence.

coverage_items.label: BRCGS logo and certification status references
coverage_items.reminder: Mention whether the BRCGS logo/certification status references are used and controlled according to the protocol.
coverage_items.original_text: 1.1.11 The BRCGS logo and references to certification status shall be used only in accordance with the conditions of use detailed in the audit protocol section (Part III, section 6.8) of the Standard.

1.1.original_text:
Fundamental

The site’s senior management shall demonstrate that they are fully committed to the implementation of the requirements of the Global Standard Packaging Materials and to processes which facilitate continual improvement of product safety, quality management, and the site’s product safety and quality culture.

1.1.1 The site shall maintain a documented policy which states the site’s intention to meet its obligation to produce safe and legally compliant products to the specified quality and confirms its responsibility to its customers. This shall:
• be signed by the person with overall responsibility for the site
• be communicated to all personnel
• include commitment to continuously improve the site’s product safety and quality culture.

1.1.2 The site’s senior management shall define and maintain a clear and effective plan for the development and continuing improvement of a product safety and quality culture. The plan shall include measures needed to achieve a positive culture change.
This shall include:
• defined activities which aim to improve and further develop product safety and quality culture. As a minimum, these activities shall be designed around:
• clear and open communication of product safety
• training
• feedback from personnel
• the behaviours required to maintain and improve product safety processes
• performance measurement of activities related to the safety, legality and quality of products
• an action plan indicating how the activities will be undertaken and measured, and the intended timescales
• a review of the effectiveness of completed and ongoing activities.
The plan shall be reviewed and updated, at a minimum, annually.

1.1.3 The company shall have a confidential reporting system to enable personnel to report concerns relating to product safety, legality, and quality.
The mechanism for reporting concerns shall be clearly communicated to all personnel.
The company’s senior management shall have a process for assessing any concerns raised. Records of the assessment and, where appropriate, actions taken, shall be documented.

1.1.4 The site’s senior management shall establish clear objectives to maintain and improve the safety, legality and quality of products manufactured, in accordance with the site’s product safety and quality policy and this Standard. These objectives shall be:
• documented and include targets or clear measures of success
• clearly communicated to relevant personnel
• monitored, and the results reported at a suitable predetermined frequency to the site’s senior management.

1.1.5 The company’s senior management shall provide the human and financial resources required for the manufacture of safe and legally compliant products, to the required quality, and in compliance with the requirements of this Standard.

1.1.6 The company’s senior management shall have a system in place to ensure that the site is kept informed of and reviews:
• scientific and technical developments
• industry codes of practice
• all relevant legislation applicable in the country of manufacture and, where known, the country where the product will be used.

1.1.7 The site shall have a genuine, original hard copy or electronic version of the current Standard and be aware of any changes to the Standard or protocol that are published on the BRCGS website and Participate.

1.1.8 Where the site is certificated to the Standard, it shall ensure that announced or blended announced re-certification audits occur on or before the audit due date indicated on the certificate.
It is the site’s responsibility to ensure that all requirements are in place to ensure that the unannounced audit can be undertaken in accordance with the protocol of the Standard (see Part III, section 4.7.1). This includes agreeing contractual terms with the certification body in advance of the start of the 4-month window, and keeping the certification body up to date on changes that may affect this planning, such as maintenance shutdowns.

1.1.9 The most senior manufacturing or operations manager on site shall participate in the opening and closing meetings of the audit for certification to the Standard.
Relevant departmental managers or their deputies shall be available as required during the audit.
A member of the senior management team on site shall be available during the audit for a discussion on effective implementation of the product safety and quality culture plan.

1.1.10 The site’s senior management shall ensure that the root causes of any non-conformities identified at the previous audit against the Standard have been effectively addressed to prevent recurrence.

1.1.11 The BRCGS logo and references to certification status shall be used only in accordance with the conditions of use detailed in the audit protocol section (Part III, section 6.8) of the Standard.

2.5.1 The HARA team shall identify and record all the potential hazards that are reasonably expected to occur at each manufacturing process step, and consideration of the following types of hazards:
• microbiological
• physical
• chemical
The HARA shall take into account, the potential for:
• migration of substances
• issues arising from the use of recycled materials
• limitations of use of the product
• foreseeable unintended use by the customer or consumer
• defects critical to consumer safety
• hazards that may have an impact on the functional integrity and performance of the final product in use
• malicious intervention
• raw material fraud (e.g., substitution, adulteration or misrepresentation)
• allergen contamination risks.

• likelihood of occurrence, considering prerequisite programs in the absence of additional control
• severity of the outcome.

2.5.1 The HARA team shall identify and record all the potential hazards that are reasonably expected to occur at each manufacturing process step, and consideration of the following types of hazards:
• microbiological

The HARA shall take into account, the potential for:

• issues arising from the use of recycled materials
• limitations of use of the product
• foreseeable unintended use by the customer or consumer
• defects critical to consumer safety
• hazards that may have an impact on the functional integrity and performance of the final product in use
• malicious intervention
• raw material fraud (e.g., substitution, adulteration or misrepresentation)

2.5.3 The HARA team shall consider the control measures necessary to prevent or eliminate each product safety hazard or reduce it to an acceptable level.

In order to minimise the risk of infestation and risk to products, the whole site shall have an effective preventive pest management programme in place and the resources available to respond immediately to any issues which occur.

4.11.1 A preventive pest management programme shall be maintained, covering all areas of the site under the site’s control.
The site shall assess the suitability of its pest management programme to address variation in pest activity through different seasons, and consider any additional preventive activity required.
The site shall document and implement any required additional activity.

4.11.2 The site shall either contract the services of a competent pest management organisation or have appropriately trained personnel for the regular inspection and treatment of the site in order to deter and eradicate infestation. The frequency of inspections shall be determined by risk assessment and documented. The risk assessment shall be reviewed whenever:
• there are changes to the building or manufacturing processes which could have an impact on the pest management programme
• there has been a significant pest issue.
Where the services of a pest management contractor are employed, the service contract shall be clearly defined and reflect the activities of the site and comply with local legislation as required.

4.11.3 Where a site undertakes its own pest management, it shall be able to demonstrate that:
• pest management operations are undertaken by trained and competent personnel with sufficient knowledge to select appropriate pest control chemicals and proofing methods and understand the limitations of use, relevant to the biology of the pests associated with the site
• personnel undertaking pest management activities meet any legal requirements for training or registration
• sufficient resources are available to respond to any infestation issues
• there is ready access to specialist technical knowledge when required
• legislation governing the use of pest control products is understood and complied with.

4.11.4 Equipment such as bait stations, traps or electric fly-killing devices shall be appropriately located and operational.
Where pest control products are stored on site, dedicated locked facilities shall be used.

4.11.5 Effective precautions shall be in place to prevent pests entering the premises. The building shall be suitably proofed against the entry of all pests via doors, windows, ducts, drains and cable entry points.
This shall include measures to prevent birds and flying mammals from entering buildings or roosting above loading or unloading areas.

4.11.6 In the event of infestation, immediate action shall be taken to eliminate the hazard. Action shall be taken to identify, evaluate the potential for contamination or damage, and authorise the release of any product potentially affected.

• clearly defined responsibilities for the site management and the contractor
• details of pest control products used and instructions for their effective use
• detailed records of inspections, recommendations and of any pest infestation.

4.9.title: Product contamination control
4.9.original_text:
All practicable steps shall be taken to identify, eliminate, avoid or minimise the risk of foreign-body, chemical or allergen contamination.

4.9.1 Glass and brittle materials control

4.9.1.1 There shall be no unnecessary non-manufacturing glass or other brittle materials present, which may pose a foreseeable risk of contamination.
Where non-manufacturing glass or other brittle materials are required in manufacturing, packing or storage areas, and where there is a risk of product contamination, systems for their safe use shall be in place.
Systems for cleaning or replacing the above items shall be in place to minimise the potential for product contamination.

4.9.1.2 Glass or other brittle materials (other than the product) that pose a potential product contamination hazard shall be controlled and recorded on a register that includes, as a minimum:
• a list of items detailing location, number, type and condition
• recorded checks of condition of items, carried out at a specified frequency that is based on the level of risk to the product
Glass or brittle materials not in the manufacturing or storage areas shall be included in the register based on risk.

4.9.1.3 Where non-manufacturing glass or brittle materials breakage occurs, a responsible person shall be placed in charge of the clean-up operation and shall ensure that no other area is allowed to become contaminated due to the breakage. Any product that has become contaminated shall be segregated and disposed of.
All breakages shall be recorded in an incident report.

4.9.2 Sharps and metal control

4.9.2.1 There shall be a procedure for the controlled use and storage of sharp implements, including knives, blades, needles and wires, to prevent product contamination.
The procedure shall include:
• issue and control of sharp implements in the manufacturing, storage and ancillary areas, such as engineering workshops and laboratories
• record of replacement or breakage.
Snap-off blade knives shall not be used.

4.9.2.2 Manufacturing equipment that incorporates blades or sharps shall be controlled and monitored. Blades or other sharp implements shall not be allowed to contaminate the product.

4.9.3 Chemical control

4.9.3.1 Procedures shall be in place to manage the use, storage and handling of non-manufacturing chemicals, such as lubricants and cleaning chemicals to prevent product contamination. These shall include, as a minimum:
• a register of approved chemicals for purchase
• confirmation of suitability, including food or hygiene sensitive contact
• use in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions
• availability of material safety data sheets and specifications
• avoidance of strongly scented products, where potential risks of taint contamination may occur
• the labelling and/or identification of containers of chemicals at all times
• designated storage with access restricted to authorised personnel
• procedures to manage any spills
• use by trained personnel only.

4.9.4 Allergen Management

4.9.4.1 Where a potential for contamination from allergen or intrinsic allergenic components has been identified as part of the HARA, the site shall establish, implement, and maintain an allergen management plan. This plan shall minimise or eliminate the risk of contamination to and/or from the product. The plan shall meet legal requirements for labelling in the country of sale.
The plan shall be reviewed based on risk, such as changes to manufacturing operations, personnel changes, raw materials and lubricants.

4.9.4.2 Where an allergen risk is identified, appropriate controls shall be established and implemented to eliminate or reduce the risk, through personnel training, raw material specifications, segregation and handling.

4.9.5 Other physical contaminants

4.9.5.1 Notices on equipment shall be cleanable and secure and shall not pose a risk to product safety, legality and quality.

4.9.5.2 Where it poses a risk to product, wooden equipment including desks, chairs, tables, etc., shall be properly sealed to enable effective cleaning. This equipment shall be kept clean, in good condition and free from splinters or other sources of physical contamination.

4.9.5.3 Staples, paper clips and drawing pins shall not be used in open product areas.
Where staples or other items are present as packing materials or closures, appropriate precautions shall be taken to minimise the risk of product contamination.

4.9.5.4 Site issued portable handheld equipment, e.g., mobile phones, tablets, measuring equipment and similar portable items, shall be controlled by the site to minimise the risk of physical contamination.

4.9.5.5 Based on risk, procedures shall be implemented to minimise other types of foreign body contamination (i.e., types of contamination that are not specifically covered elsewhere in section 4.9).
